title: Ladakh packing guide for men
description: What men should pack for Ladakh: the layering system, a packing list by trip length, altitude tips, and three budgets with real brands.
intro: Ladakh is high, dry, and cold at night, even in summer. The sun burns your skin by noon and the wind freezes you by evening. You dress in layers, not in one big jacket. Pack three layers: a base, a warm mid, and a windproof shell. This guide covers the system, a packing list by trip length, three budget looks with real brands, and a few altitude notes that matter more than any jacket.

sections.heading: The three-layer system
sections.body: A base layer wicks sweat. A mid layer traps heat. A shell blocks wind and rain. You take layers off as the sun rises and put them back at dusk. Cotton is the wrong fabric because it holds sweat and gets cold. Choose merino or synthetic thermals for the base, fleece or a light down jacket for the mid, and a windproof jacket for the shell. A neck gaiter, gloves, and a beanie weigh little and make a big difference.
tips: Base: merino or synthetic thermal top and leggings.
Mid: fleece or light down jacket.
Shell: windproof and water-resistant jacket with a hood.
Extras: beanie, gloves, neck gaiter, UV sunglasses, SPF 50.

sections.heading: Climate note
sections.body: Ladakh sits above 3,000 metres. In June to September, days are 15 to 25 degrees and nights fall to 5 or lower. Passes like Khardung La can be below freezing. In April and October, nights drop below zero. The air is thin and dry. UV is strong. Sunburn comes fast, even on a cold day. Drink more water than you think you need. Moisturise your lips and skin. Take it easy on the first two days.

sections.heading: Packing list by trip length
sections.body: Ladakh trips run longer, because you need to acclimatise. You will not wash often. Pack layers you can re-wear. Wear the bulkiest items on the plane. Leh has shops for gear but prices are higher and the stock is limited.
tips: 5 to 6 days: 2 thermals, 3 tees, 2 trousers, 1 fleece, 1 down jacket, 1 shell, 4 pairs of socks.
8 to 10 days: 3 thermals, 4 tees, 3 trousers, 1 fleece, 1 down jacket, 1 shell, 6 pairs of socks.
All trips: beanie, gloves, neck gaiter, UV sunglasses, sunscreen, lip balm, trekking shoes, sandals for the hotel.

sections.heading: Three looks by budget
sections.body: Prices are approximate. Decathlon and Wildcraft are common in India. Uniqlo has good thermals and down layers.

looks.name: Basic layers, tight budget
looks.budget_inr: under 1,500 for the thermal and fleece
looks.why: Thermal plus fleece, with your own windcheater, is enough for most days in summer.

looks.name: Proper kit, mid range
pieces: Uniqlo ultra light down jacket, about ₹5,000
looks.budget_inr: 1,500 to 4,000 for the thermal and shell each
looks.why: A down jacket and a shell keep you warm on the passes and pack small.

looks.name: Serious cold, upper range
looks.budget_inr: 4,000 to 10,000 for the base layer and jacket
looks.why: Go this way if you travel in April or October, or if you ride a bike through the passes.

tips: Test every layer before the trip, not at the first pass.
Break in the shoes. New shoes and long walks do not mix.

sections.heading: Wear on the plane
sections.body: Wear your heaviest layers, trekking shoes, and trousers. Put the down jacket on, since the flight into Leh is cold on landing. Keep your thermals and a beanie in your carry-on. Wear a tee you can take off. The sun is strong in the morning. Do not pack the down jacket in checked luggage. Bags can be delayed.

sections.heading: Altitude and common mistakes
sections.body: Rest for the first 24 to 48 hours in Leh. Walk slowly and drink water. Avoid alcohol on arrival. If you get a headache, nausea, or dizziness, rest and tell your guide. Do not ignore these signs. Common packing mistakes are too much cotton, no sun protection, and new shoes. Bring a power bank, because cold drains your phone battery quickly.

sections.heading: Day by day: how the layers change
sections.body: A typical day starts cold. At 6 a.m. you wear a thermal, a fleece, and a shell. By 10 a.m. the sun is strong, so you remove the fleece and wear a tee under the shell. At a high pass, put the fleece and the down jacket back on, since the wind chills you in seconds. By 4 p.m. the sun drops and so does the temperature. At night, wear the down jacket, a beanie, and warm socks. Keep a small daypack to carry what you take off. Change your socks daily, because damp feet get cold. Dry your base layers on a hotel radiator or a chair, away from the heater.

sections.heading: What to stop buying
sections.body: Stop buying cotton hoodies for Ladakh. Stop buying fashion jackets with no wind protection. Stop buying a large jacket when layers are better. Buy thermals, a shell, and good socks.

faq.q: What should men pack for Ladakh?
faq.a: Thermals, a fleece, a down jacket, a windproof shell, trousers, thick socks, a beanie, gloves, sunglasses, and sunscreen.

faq.q: Is it cold in Ladakh in summer?
faq.a: Days are mild but nights fall to around 5 degrees. The passes are colder. Pack layers.

faq.q: Can I buy winter clothes in Leh?
faq.a: Yes, but prices are higher and the sizes are limited. Buy the main items before you travel.

faq.q: What shoes are best for Ladakh?
faq.a: Waterproof trekking shoes with good grip, broken in before the trip. Carry sandals for the hotel.
